Samech
SAH-mek
n. (the fifteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet; the heading of the fifteenth stanza of Psalm 119)
Hebrew samek, a prop or support, the fifteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet; rendered Samech by the Authorized Version in Psalm 119.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Samech is the fifteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet and heads the fifteenth stanza of Psalm 119: “SAMECH. I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love” (Psalm 119:113). The letter's name is a prop, the thing set under a weight to hold it up, and the stanza is about what a man leans on. Having set his hatred against empty thinking, the psalmist names his refuge: “Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word” (Psalm 119:114). The prop is not his resolve but God Himself, and the holding is God's work: “Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope” (Psalm 119:116). A believer upheld by God does not therefore grow careless of God; the stanza ends in trembling: “My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments” (Psalm 119:120). Love and fear stand together here without apology. The man who hates vanity, loves the law, hides in God, is held up by God, and shakes before God's judgments is one man and not four, and the fifteenth letter names what carries him.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Samech is the name of a Hebrew letter and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Samech is the name of the fifteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The Authorized Version prints it as the heading of Psalm 119:113.

The Hebrew name denotes a prop or support.

Its stanza joins love of the law to the fear of God's judgments.

The stanza runs from Psalm 119:113 to Psalm 119:120.

Key Scripture

Psa 119:113 — "SAMECH. I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love."

Psa 119:114 — "Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word."

Psa 119:116 — "Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope."

Psa 119:120 — "My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments."

Modern Corruption

The fear of God is treated as incompatible with loving Him; under Samech one man both loves the law and trembles at the judgments.

expand to see more

It is widely assumed that a God truly loved cannot be truly feared, and that trembling belongs to an immature faith. The fifteenth stanza of Psalm 119 puts love and dread in the same mouth without embarrassment. The man who says he hates vain thoughts and loves the law is the same man whose flesh trembles for fear of God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God Himself is the prop under a believer's life, that he is upheld by promise and not by resolve, and that filial fear is part of love, not its enemy.
